proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(f(u)=\sum_q b_{tq,\ell}{\bf 1}\{u>s_{tq,\ell}\}\) and abbreviate \(b_q=b_{tq,\ell}\), \(s_q=s_{tq,\ell}\).  Since \(s_q\in[0,1]\), Tonelli's theorem for this finite sum gives
\[
 \|f\|_2^2
 =\sum_{q,q'}b_qb_{q'}\int_0^1{\bf 1}\{u>s_q\}{\bf 1}\{u>s_{q'}\}\,du
 =\sum_{q,q'}b_qb_{q'}\{1-\max(s_q,s_{q'})\}.
\]
The constant term is \((\sum_qb_q)^2=0\).  Using
\(\max(x,y)=(x+y+|x-y|)/2\), the two linear terms are
\[
 -\frac12\sum_{q,q'}b_qb_{q'}(s_q+s_{q'})
 =-\Big(\sum_qb_qs_q\Big)\Big(\sum_{q'}b_{q'}\Big)=0.
\]
Thus
\[
 \|f\|_2^2=-\frac12\sum_{q,q'}b_qb_{q'}|s_q-s_{q'}|.
\]
This also proves nonnegativity of the right-hand side without an additional assumption.

For a discrete law with ordered support \(x_1\leq\cdots\leq x_R\), cumulative masses \(c_r\), and jumps \(\Delta_r=x_{r+1}-x_r\), its generalized inverse satisfies, outside the finite knot set,
\[
 Q(u)=x_1+\sum_{r<R}\Delta_r{\bf 1}\{u>c_r\},\qquad
 \widehat Q(u)-Q(u)=\sum_{r<R}\Delta_r
 \bigl({\bf 1}\{u>\widehat c_r\}-{\bf 1}\{u>c_r\}\bigr).
\]
This remains true when a population atom is unobserved, because retaining it with empirical mass zero makes the adjacent intervals telescope.  By \(\mathrm{ass:finite\mbox{-}post}\), there are finitely many terms.  Applying the displayed representation to the treated empirical error with coefficient \(-1\) and to donor \(j\) with coefficient \(w_{\ell j}\) produces exactly the separately anchored list in \(\mathrm{def:finite\mbox{-}endpoint\mbox{-}energy}\).  Every jump contributes \(a\) and \(-a\), so its total coefficient is zero.  Hence
\[
 \|D^{\mathrm{post}}_{t,\ell}\|_2^2
 =-\frac12\sum_{q,q'}b_{tq,\ell}b_{tq',\ell}
 |s_{tq,\ell}-s_{tq',\ell}|
 =m_\ell^{-1/2}\Psi^{\mathrm{fin}}_{t,\ell}.
\]

Aggregate the coefficients at each distinct endpoint \(z\) as \(B(z)=\sum_{q:s_q=z}b_q\).  Ordered from left to right, the value of \(f\) between two consecutive endpoints is the cumulative sum of the preceding \(B(z)\)'s.  Therefore \(f=0\) almost everywhere if every \(B(z)=0\).  Conversely, if \(f=0\) almost everywhere, successive differences of these interval values show \(B(z)=0\) at every endpoint below one; the condition \(\sum_qb_q=0\) then gives the same conclusion at the endpoint one.  This proves the asserted equivalence.

Finally, if \(\delta=\max_q|s_q-s'_q|\), the reverse triangle inequality yields
\[
 \big||s_q-s_{q'}|-|s'_q-s'_{q'}|\big|
 \leq |s_q-s'_q|+|s_{q'}-s'_{q'}|\leq2\delta.
\]
Consequently
\[
 |\Psi(s)-\Psi(s')|
 \leq\frac12\sum_{q,q'}|b_qb_{q'}|,2\delta
 =\Big(\sum_q|b_q|\Big)^2\delta,
\]
as required.

By \(\mathrm{ass:stable\mbox{-}quantile\mbox{-}span}\), for every post period,
\[
 \widehat\tau_{t,\ell}-\tau_{t,\ell}
 =D^{\mathrm{post}}_{t,\ell}
 -\sum_{j=1}^J(\widehat w_{\ell j}-w_{\ell j})Q_{jt,\ell}
 -\sum_{j=1}^J(\widehat w_{\ell j}-w_{\ell j})
   (\widehat Q_{jt,\ell}-Q_{jt,\ell}).
\]
If \(\widehat w_\ell=w_\ell\), the last two terms vanish.  The conclusion
\(E_{t,\ell}=m_\ell^{-1/2}\Psi^{\mathrm{fin}}_{t,\ell}\) then follows from \(\mathrm{lem:endpoint\mbox{-}identity}\).

If every observed post law is a point mass, a sample from any such cell equals its support point with probability one.  Thus all post empirical quantiles equal their population quantiles, \(D^{\mathrm{post}}_{t,\ell}=0\), and \(\epsilon_{t,\ell}=0\).  There are no nonzero jumps, so \(\Psi^{\mathrm{fin}}_{t,\ell}=0\).  The preceding display becomes
\[
 \widehat\tau_{t,\ell}-\tau_{t,\ell}
 =-(\widehat w_\ell-w_\ell)^\top q_{t,\ell},
\]
and hence, by \(\mathrm{def:finite\mbox{-}weight\mbox{-}quadratic}\),
\[
 E_{t,\ell}=(\widehat w_\ell-w_\ell)^\top M_{t,\ell}
 (\widehat w_\ell-w_\ell)
 =n_\ell^{-1}A_{t,\ell}\bigl(\sqrt{n_\ell}
 (\widehat w_\ell-w_\ell)\bigr).
\]
Both restrictions together make the displayed error identically zero.

Let \(K\leq (J+1)T_1(S-1)\) be the total number of retained post knots.  It is fixed by \(\mathrm{ass:fixed\mbox{-}panel}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:finite\mbox{-}post}\).  For each of the finitely many ordered pairs \((a,b)\) of knots, the sequence
\(\sqrt{m_\ell}(c_{a,\ell}-c_{b,\ell})\) takes values in the compact extended line \([-\infty,\infty]\).  Successive finite subsequence extractions therefore make all these differences converge simultaneously.  Declare \(a\sim b\) when the limit is finite.  Since exact differences add before taking a finite limit, this is an equivalence relation.  Its classes are the macro clusters.  Within a class choose one knot as origin; the limits relative to that origin are the offsets \(d\).  Between different classes the absolute scaled difference diverges.

Each \(\sqrt{n_\ell}w_{\ell j}\) lies in \([0,\infty]\), and \(\rho_\ell\) lies in the same compactified half-line.  A further finite diagonal extraction gives all limits \(h_j\) and the limit of \(\rho_\ell\).  Because \(\sum_j\sqrt{n_\ell}w_{\ell j}=\sqrt{n_\ell}\to\infty\) by \(\mathrm{ass:sample\mbox{-}divergence}\), at least one coordinate of \(h\) is infinite.

All quantile functions take values in the common compact outcome interval of length \(D\).  Translate that fixed interval once, which does not change differences or any quadratic restricted to \(L\), and regard the functions as bounded in \([0,D]\).  A bounded sequence of monotone functions has a pointwise-convergent subsequence at every continuity point of a monotone limit: this follows by diagonal extraction on the rationals followed by monotonicity.  The discontinuity set is countable, so dominated convergence gives \(L^2\) convergence.  Applying this argument to the finitely many donor--period sequences produces \(q_{t,\ell}\to q_t\) in \(L^2([0,1])^J\).  Therefore, by Cauchy--Schwarz,
\[
 \|M_{t,\ell}-M_t\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq \|q_{t,\ell}-q_t\|_2
       (\|q_{t,\ell}\|_2+\|q_t\|_2)\longrightarrow0.
\]
The same boundedness makes the entries of \(H_\ell\) lie in a fixed compact interval, so another finite extraction gives \(H_\ell\to H\).  Atom locations, masses, jumps, and the finitely many multinomial covariance entries are bounded; hence they too have joint convergent subsubsequences.  These extractions can be nested because their number is finite.

For any \(v\in L\), \(\mathrm{ass:strong\mbox{-}gram}\) and entrywise convergence give
\[
 v^\top Hv=\lim_\ell v^\top H_\ell v
 \geq\lambda\|v\|_2^2.
\]
No local convergence condition has been imposed on the original array: the coordinates were obtained only after selecting a limit point from each compactified finite-dimensional sequence.

Write \(\widehat q_{t,\ell}=(\widehat Q_{1t,\ell},\ldots,
\widehat Q_{Jt,\ell})^\top\) in the pre periods, and use the pooled norm
\(\|z\|_\pi^2=\sum_{t\leq T_0}\pi_t\int_0^1z_t(u)^2du\).
On the simultaneous empirical-CDF event with width \(x\), the density lower bound in \(\mathrm{ass:smooth\mbox{-}pre}\) implies
\[
 \max_{j,t}\|\widehat Q_{jt,\ell}-Q_{jt,\ell}\|_\infty
 \vee\max_t\|\widehat Q^N_{0t,\ell}-Q^N_{0t,\ell}\|_\infty
 \leq x/f_{\min}.
\]
The cited DKW bound, with a finite union over cells, makes the left side \(O_{\Pr}(n_\ell^{-1/2})\) uniformly over \(\mathcal M\).  Let \(e_\ell\) denote this maximum and \(\delta_\ell=\widehat w_\ell-w_\ell\).  Exact span and empirical optimality give
\[
 \|\widehat q_\ell^\top\delta_\ell\|_\pi
 \leq \|\widehat Q^N_{0,\ell}-\widehat q_\ell^\top w_\ell\|_\pi
 +\|\widehat Q^N_{0,\ell}-\widehat q_\ell^\top\widehat w_\ell\|_\pi
 \leq4e_\ell.
\]
Since \(\delta_\ell\in L\), the population curvature and
\(\|\delta_\ell\|_1\leq\sqrt J\|\delta_\ell\|_2\) yield
\[
 \sqrt\lambda\|\delta_\ell\|_2
 \leq\|q_\ell^\top\delta_\ell\|_\pi
 \leq4e_\ell+\sqrt J e_\ell\|\delta_\ell\|_2.
\]
For all sufficiently large \(\ell\), uniformly in the law, the last coefficient is smaller than \(\sqrt\lambda/2\) with arbitrarily high probability.  This proves
\(\|\widehat w_\ell-w_\ell\|_2=O_{\Pr}(n_\ell^{-1/2})\) uniformly.

For the limit, set
\[
 D_\ell=\{v\in L:v_j\geq-\sqrt{n_\ell}w_{\ell j}\},
 \quad
 \widehat H_\ell=\sum_{t\leq T_0}\pi_t\int_0^1
 \widehat q_{t,\ell}\widehat q_{t,\ell}^\top,
\]
and
\[
 \widehat g_\ell=\sum_{t\leq T_0}\pi_t\int_0^1
 \widehat q_{t,\ell}(u)\sqrt{n_\ell}
 \{\widehat Q^N_{0t,\ell}(u)-\widehat q_{t,\ell}(u)^\top w_\ell\}\,du.
\]
Expanding the empirical criterion at \(w_\ell\) gives the exact identity
\[
 n_\ell\{\widehat L_\ell(w_\ell+v/\sqrt{n_\ell})-
 \widehat L_\ell(w_\ell)\}=v^\top\widehat H_\ell v-2v^\top\widehat g_\ell,
 \qquad v\in D_\ell.
\]
The empirical-CDF functional central limit theorem and the inverse-map delta method, applied using \(f\geq f_{\min}>0\) and the derivative bound in \(\mathrm{ass:smooth\mbox{-}pre}\), give jointly
\[
 \widehat H_\ell\to H,\qquad \widehat g_\ell\Rightarrow g.
\]
The inversion derivative is obtained directly from
\((F+t z)(Q+t k)=u+o(t)\): uniform Taylor expansion gives
\(f(Q)k+z(Q)=0\), hence \(k=-z(Q)/f(Q)\).  Cell independence makes the contributing bridges independent.

Coordinatewise convergence of the bounds defining \(D_\ell\) gives Painleve--Kuratowski convergence \(D_\ell\to D_h\).  Explicitly, limits of bounded \(v_\ell\in D_\ell\) lie in \(D_h\).  Conversely, clip any \(v\in D_h\) inward by \(o(1)\) at the finitely constrained coordinates and restore the sum-zero equality through a coordinate with \(h_j=\infty\), whose existence was proved in \(\mathrm{lem:local\mbox{-}subsequence\mbox{-}extraction}\).  The resulting \(v_\ell\in D_\ell\) converges to \(v\).

Strong convexity gives the deterministic argmin step.  Indeed, comparison with the feasible point zero bounds every minimizer by \(2\|\widehat g_\ell\|/\lambda+o_{\Pr}(1)\); every convergent subsubsequence then satisfies the limiting variational inequality, and uniqueness forces its limit to be
\[
 V_h=\operatorname*{argmin}_{v\in D_h}\{v^\top Hv-2v^\top g\}.
\]
Thus \(\sqrt{n_\ell}(\widehat w_\ell-w_\ell)\Rightarrow V_h\).

It remains to prove the two zero characterizations.  For \(a\in L\setminus\{0\}\), strong Gram curvature implies that \(a^\top q_t\) is nonzero in \(L^2\) for at least one pre period.  The treated-cell bridge in the score is independent of all donor bridges and has strictly positive variance against this nonzero integrand because its density is positive.  Hence \(a^\top g\) has positive variance.  Thus the Gaussian score has full support on \(L\).  Projection under the positive definite metric \(H|_L\) consequently gives \(\operatorname{supp}(V_h)=D_h\).  Moreover \(D_h\) spans \(L\): at least one constraint is absent, and a sufficiently small relative-interior neighborhood in the remaining coordinates spans the sum-zero space.

Now
\[
 A_t(v)=v^\top M_tv=\Big\|\sum_{j=1}^Jv_jQ_{jt}\Big\|_2^2.
\]
Therefore \(A_t(V_h)=0\) almost surely iff \(D_h\subseteq\ker M_t\), equivalently \(L\subseteq\ker M_t\).  The latter holds iff
\(Q_{jt}-Q_{kt}=0\) almost everywhere for every \(j,k\), which is precisely equality of all donor post quantiles.  Finally, the inverse image of the relative interior of each nonempty polyhedral face \(F\) under the metric projection contains the full-dimensional set
\(H\operatorname{relint}(F)+N_{D_h}(F)\), so it has positive Gaussian probability.  Conditional on projection to \(F\), the relative-interior component has a density.  Hence that face contributes positive mass to \(A_t(V_h)=0\) iff the quadratic vanishes throughout \(F\), namely iff \(F\subseteq\ker M_t\).

Let \(\delta_\ell=\widehat w_\ell-w_\ell=v_\ell/\sqrt{n_\ell}\), write \(D=D_{t,\ell}\), \(q=q_{t,\ell}\), and \(\epsilon=\epsilon_{t,\ell}\).  Exact stable span gives, without a limiting argument,
\[
 \widehat\tau_{t,\ell}-\tau_{t,\ell}
 =D-\delta_\ell^\top q-\delta_\ell^\top\epsilon.
\]
Squaring this equality in \(L^2([0,1])\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E_{t,\ell}={}&\|D\|_2^2+\|\delta_\ell^\top q\|_2^2
 -2\langle D,\delta_\ell^\top q\rangle+\|\delta_\ell^\top\epsilon\|_2^2\\
 &-2\langle D,\delta_\ell^\top\epsilon\rangle
 +2\langle\delta_\ell^\top q,\delta_\ell^\top\epsilon\rangle.
\end{aligned}
\]
By \(\mathrm{lem:endpoint\mbox{-}identity}\), the first term is
\(m_\ell^{-1/2}\Psi^{\mathrm{fin}}_{t,\ell}\).  The second is
\(n_\ell^{-1}A_{t,\ell}(v_\ell)\), and the third is
\[
 -2(n_\ell m_\ell)^{-1/2}v_\ell^\top
 \left\{\sqrt{m_\ell}\int_0^1q(u)D(u)du\right\}
 =-2(n_\ell m_\ell)^{-1/2}v_\ell^\top B_{t,\ell}.
\]
Substitution of \(\delta_\ell=v_\ell/\sqrt{n_\ell}\) into the last three terms gives exactly the three displayed \(\epsilon_{t,\ell}\) terms and hence the stated exact decomposition.

For the rates, the discrete quantile representation in the proof of
\(\mathrm{lem:endpoint\mbox{-}identity}\) writes every cell error as at most \(S-1\) pulses, each of height at most \(D\), with total pulse length bounded by
\[
 \sum_{r<S}|\widehat c_{jtr,\ell}-c_{jtr,\ell}|
 \leq (S-1)\|\widehat F_{jt,\ell}-F_{jt,\ell}\|_\infty.
\]
The cited DKW bound, finite \(S,J,T_1\), and simplex condition imply, uniformly and jointly in post periods,
\[
 \|\epsilon_{t,\ell}\|_{1,2}=O_{\Pr}(m_\ell^{-1/2}),\quad
 \|D_{t,\ell}\|_1=O_{\Pr}(m_\ell^{-1/2}),\quad
 \|D_{t,\ell}\|_\infty\leq2D,\quad
 \|\epsilon_{t,\ell}\|_{\infty,2}\leq\sqrt J D.
\]
The common outcome bound gives \(\|q_{t,\ell}\|_{\infty,2}\leq\sqrt J D\), while \(\mathrm{thm:face\mbox{-}weight\mbox{-}limit}\) gives \(\|v_\ell\|_2=O_{\Pr}(1)\).  It follows that
\[
 \|B_{t,\ell}\|_2
 \leq\sqrt{m_\ell}\|q_{t,\ell}\|_{\infty,2}\|D_{t,\ell}\|_1
 =O_{\Pr}(1).
\]
Using \(|\langle f,g\rangle|\leq\|f\|_1\|g\|_\infty\) rather than an \(L^2\) bound gives successively
\[
\begin{aligned}
 n_\ell^{-1}\|v_\ell^\top\epsilon\|_2^2
 &\leq n_\ell^{-1}\|v_\ell^\top\epsilon\|_1
 \|v_\ell^\top\epsilon\|_\infty
 =O_{\Pr}(n_\ell^{-1}m_\ell^{-1/2}),\\
 n_\ell^{-1/2}|\langle D,v_\ell^\top\epsilon\rangle|
 &=O_{\Pr}(n_\ell^{-1/2}m_\ell^{-1/2}),\\
 n_\ell^{-1}|\langle v_\ell^\top q,v_\ell^\top\epsilon\rangle|
 &=O_{\Pr}(n_\ell^{-1}m_\ell^{-1/2}).
\end{aligned}
\]
Together with the bound for \(B_{t,\ell}\), these are the four asserted orders.  Since
\[
 \frac{n_\ell^{-1/2}m_\ell^{-1/2}}
 {n_\ell^{-1}+m_\ell^{-1/2}}
 \leq\min(n_\ell^{-1/2},m_\ell^{-1/4})\to0
\]
and the product \(n_\ell^{-1}m_\ell^{-1/2}\) is smaller still, the exact remainder is \(o_{\Pr}(a_\ell)\).

The pre empirical processes in \(\mathrm{thm:face\mbox{-}weight\mbox{-}limit}\) and the post empirical processes are independent by \(\mathrm{ass:cell\mbox{-}independence}\).  The cited empirical-CDF functional central limit theorem therefore supplies a joint Gaussian limit \((g,Z)\) with independent pre and post blocks and the within-cell bridge covariance
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}(Z_{jtr},Z_{jtr'})=\min(c_{jtr},c_{jtr'})-c_{jtr}c_{jtr'},
 \qquad \operatorname{Cov}(Z_{jtr},Z_{j'tr'})=0\quad(j\neq j').
\]
The cited Skorokhod representation theorem permits this joint weak convergence to be realized on one probability space with almost-sure convergence; this is the coupling asserted in the statement.

Within a finite root-\(m_\ell\) knot cluster, subtracting a common translation and using
\(\sqrt{m_\ell}(\widehat c-c)=Z_\ell\) changes the separately anchored pairs to
\[
 (a,d+Z_\ell),\qquad(-a,d).
\]
Between macro clusters, pulse supports are eventually disjoint.  Thus the exact squared norm is the sum of the cluster energies.  Convergence of jump coefficients, offsets, and Gaussian coordinates, together with the separation-free Lipschitz inequality in
\(\mathrm{lem:endpoint\mbox{-}identity}\), gives jointly in \(t\)
\[
 \Psi^{\mathrm{fin}}_{t,\ell}\longrightarrow\Psi_t(d,Z).
\]
The argmin proof gives \(v_\ell\to V_h\) on the same coupling.  Since
\(M_{t,\ell}\to M_t\), continuity of a quadratic form gives
\[
 A_{t,\ell}(v_\ell)\longrightarrow V_h^\top M_tV_h=A_t(V_h).
\]
Finally, the finite post laws make \(B_{t,\ell}\) a finite sum of integrals over the same shrinking pulse intervals.  After multiplying their lengths by \(\sqrt{m_\ell}\), endpoint convergence on every local ordering cell gives the finite limit denoted by \(B_t(d,Z)\); ties have probability zero unless the corresponding affine Gaussian endpoints agree almost surely, in which case the separately anchored formula gives the same value from either adjacent cell.  Hence \(B_{t,\ell}\Rightarrow B_t(d,Z)\), jointly with the preceding limits.

The exact expansion now gives
\[
 \sqrt{n_\ell m_\ell}\left[-2(n_\ell m_\ell)^{-1/2}
 v_\ell^\top B_{t,\ell}\right]
 \Rightarrow-2V_h^\top B_t(d,Z).
\]
At the endpoint scale \(\sqrt{m_\ell}\), its coefficient is \(n_\ell^{-1/2}\); at the weight scale \(n_\ell\), it is
\(\sqrt{n_\ell/m_\ell}=\rho_\ell/\sqrt{n_\ell}\); and after division by \(a_\ell\), it is
\[
 \frac{(n_\ell m_\ell)^{-1/2}}{n_\ell^{-1}+m_\ell^{-1/2}}
 =\frac{\sqrt{n_\ell}}{n_\ell+\sqrt{m_\ell}}\longrightarrow0.
\]
The bounds in \(\mathrm{thm:finite\mbox{-}two\mbox{-}source\mbox{-}expansion}\) show that all three \(\epsilon\)-terms vanish at these same applicable scales.  Moreover
\[
 \frac{n_\ell^{-1}}{a_\ell}=\frac{\sqrt{m_\ell}}{n_\ell+\sqrt{m_\ell}}=1-\omega_\ell,\qquad
 \frac{m_\ell^{-1/2}}{a_\ell}=\frac{n_\ell}{n_\ell+\sqrt{m_\ell}}=\omega_\ell.
\]
Slutsky's theorem therefore yields
\[
 \frac{E_{t,\ell}}{a_\ell}\Rightarrow
 (1-\omega)A_t(V_h)+\omega\Psi_t(d,Z).
\]
Taking respectively \(\rho_\ell\to\infty\), \(\rho_\ell\to\kappa\in(0,\infty)\), and \(\rho_\ell\to0\) gives
\[
 \sqrt{m_\ell}E_{t,\ell}\Rightarrow\Psi_t(d,Z),\qquad
 \sqrt{m_\ell}E_{t,\ell}\Rightarrow\Psi_t(d,Z)+\kappa^{-1}A_t(V_h),
\]
and
\[
 n_\ell E_{t,\ell}\Rightarrow A_t(V_h),
\]
because in the last case the endpoint coefficient is \(\rho_\ell\to0\).

For endpoint degeneracy, apply the exact zero criterion to the finite affine Gaussian endpoint list.  Two endpoints from different almost-sure equality classes coincide with probability zero, since their difference is a nonzero affine Gaussian variable.  Finiteness then shows that the realized equality partition equals the almost-sure partition with probability one.  Hence \(\Psi_t=0\) almost surely exactly when the coefficients sum to zero within every almost-sure equality class.  The quadratic criterion is the one proved in \(\mathrm{thm:face\mbox{-}weight\mbox{-}limit}\).

Let \(K_n=(J+1)T_0\) and \(K_m=(J+1)T_1\).  By the cited DKW inequality and a union bound, with probability at least \(1-\alpha/2\), every pre empirical CDF is within \(\varepsilon_{n,\ell}\) of its law; independently, with probability at least \(1-\alpha/2\), the analogous post event holds with width \(\varepsilon_{m,\ell}\).  Their intersection therefore has probability at least \(1-\alpha\).

On the pre event, inversion and \(f\geq f_{\min}\) give the common quantile bound
\(\eta_n=\varepsilon_{n,\ell}/f_{\min}\).  Repeating the empirical-optimality calculation from \(\mathrm{thm:face\mbox{-}weight\mbox{-}limit}\) without asymptotics yields
\[
 (\sqrt\lambda-\sqrt J\eta_n)\|\widehat w_\ell-w_\ell\|_2\leq4\eta_n.
\]
If the coefficient is positive, this and the simplex diameter bound
\(\|\widehat w_\ell-w_\ell\|_2\leq\sqrt2\) give exactly \(R_{w,\ell}\); if it is nonpositive, the simplex bound gives the declared fallback value.

For laws supported on an interval of length \(D\), one-dimensional transport identities and the post DKW event give
\[
 W_2^2(\widehat F,F)=\int_0^1|\widehat Q-Q|^2
 \leq D\int_0^1|\widehat Q-Q|
 =D\int_{\mathbb R}|\widehat F-F|
 \leq D^2\varepsilon_{m,\ell}.
\]
The triangle inequality, simplex weights, and
\(\|x\|_1\leq\sqrt J\|x\|_2\) therefore imply simultaneously in all post periods
\[
 \|\widehat\tau_{t,\ell}-\tau_{t,\ell}\|_2
 \leq2D\sqrt{\varepsilon_{m,\ell}}+D\sqrt J R_{w,\ell}.
\]
The deterministic bound \(2D\) supplies the outer minimum in
\(R^{\mathrm{DKW}}_\ell\).  Thus the stated ball covers on the intersection event and has finite-sample coverage at least \(1-\alpha\).  Since the fixed constants make
\(\varepsilon_{n,\ell}=O(n_\ell^{-1/2})\),
\(R_{w,\ell}=O(n_\ell^{-1/2})\), and
\(\sqrt{\varepsilon_{m,\ell}}=O(m_\ell^{-1/4})\), its diameter has the asserted uniform order.

We prove the corrected converse under its explicit richness conditions.  In the post subexperiment, keep pre laws, donors, and weights fixed and let the treated intervention law on two support points distance \(d>0\) apart have lower-atom mass \(1/2\) under \(P_0\) and \(1/2+h/\sqrt{m_\ell}\) under \(P_1\).  The two targets have squared \(L^2\) distance \(d^2h/\sqrt{m_\ell}\), hence distance \(d\sqrt h,m_\ell^{-1/4}\).  The product Hellinger affinity tends to a positive constant, since the one-observation squared Hellinger distance is \(O(h^2/m_\ell)\).  Thus the product total variation is bounded strictly below one for sufficiently small fixed \(h>0\).

For the pre subexperiment, use the two donor quantiles required by the proposed claim and let the treated pre quantile be their convex combination with weights \(w\) and \(w+h/\sqrt{n_\ell}\).  The quantile derivatives are bounded away from zero and have uniformly bounded derivatives.  Differentiating the inverse formula shows that the corresponding density score in \(w\) is bounded on the compact support; Taylor's formula therefore gives one-observation Kullback--Leibler divergence \(O(h^2/n_\ell)\), and the product Hellinger distance is bounded away from one for small fixed \(h\).  Keep the observed post laws fixed but take two donor post quantiles with \(L^2\) distance \(d_0>0\).  Exact stable span then makes the two causal targets differ by \(h d_0/\sqrt{n_\ell}\).

For either pair, let \(C_\ell\) be a confidence set honest at both laws and let \(\Delta_\ell\) be their target distance.  On the event that both targets belong to \(C_\ell\), its diameter is at least \(\Delta_\ell\).  Changing the second coverage event to the first law gives the elementary bound
\[
 P_0\{\operatorname{diam}(C_\ell)\geq\Delta_\ell\}
 \geq1-P_0\{\tau_0\notin C_\ell\}-P_1\{\tau_1\notin C_\ell\}
 -\|P_1-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}.
\]
For small fixed \(h\), the right side is positive because \(\alpha<1/2\).  This excludes the corresponding little-oh diameter order.  When both subexperiments are contained in \(\mathcal M\), it excludes little-oh of the maximum of the two rates; since their maximum and sum differ by at most a factor two, it proves the corrected combined lower bound.

The corrected statement fixes the coverage level at \(0.95\).  With \(J=1\), the simplex is \(\Delta_1=\{1\}\), so the empirical minimization cannot change the weight: \(\widehat w_\ell=w_\ell=1\) and \(v_\ell=0\).  Every term containing \(v_\ell\), including the weight quadratic, the \(B_{t,\ell}\) term, and all three \(\epsilon_{t,\ell}\) remainder terms, is therefore identically zero.

Let the treated population knot be \(1/2\), the donor knot be
\(1/2+h_B/\sqrt{m_\ell}\), and let
\(Z_0,Z_1\) be the independent limits of their centered empirical knots.  The multinomial central limit theorem gives
\(Z_0,Z_1\sim N(0,1/4)\).  The four separately anchored pairs have coefficients and local endpoints
\[
 (-1,Z_0),\quad(1,0),\quad(1,h_B+Z_1),\quad(-1,h_B).
\]
Substitution into \(-\tfrac12\sum_{q,q'}b_qb_{q'}|s_q-s_{q'}|\) and collection of the six unordered pairs gives
\[
 \Psi^B_{h_B}=|Z_0-h_B-Z_1|+|Z_0|+|Z_1|-|Z_0-h_B|-|h_B+Z_1|+h_B.
\]

For completeness, put \(S=Z_1-Z_0\) and \(R=Z_1+Z_0\).  These variables are independent \(N(0,1/2)\).  If \(h_B+S\geq0\), direct comparison of the true interval with the empirical signed interval gives
\[
 \Psi^B_{h_B}=\max\{|S|,\min(|R|,2h_B+S)\}.
\]
If \(S=-A<-h_B\), reversing the empirical interval gives
\[
 \Psi^B_{h_B}=A+\min\{2\min(h_B,A-h_B),(A-|R|)_+\}.
\]
These identities follow by ordering the four endpoints in each case and summing the constant squared error on the intervening intervals; they also follow by expanding the preceding six-term formula.

Let \(P(x)=\Phi(\sqrt2x)\), \(G(x)=2P(x)-1\), and
\(f(x)=e^{-x^2}/\sqrt\pi\).  Conditioning on \(S\), using independence of \(R\), and splitting at the two displayed order changes yields, for \(q>0\),
\[
 F_h(q):=\Pr(\Psi^B_h\leq q)=G(q)^2,\qquad h\geq q,
\]
and, for \(0\leq h<q\),
\[
 a(h,q)=\max\{q-2h,(q+2h)/3\},
\]
\[
 F_h(q)=2P(q)^2-1+2\{1-P(q)\}P(q-2h)
 -\int_{a(h,q)}^q f(z)G(2z-q)\,dz. \tag{1}
\]
This is the claimed one-dimensional Gaussian integral.  When
\(0\leq h\leq q/4\), the lower endpoint is \(q-2h\), and differentiation under the integral gives
\[
 \frac{\partial F_h(q)}{\partial h}
 =-4\{1-P(q)\}f(q-2h)-2f(q-2h)G(q-4h)\leq0.
\]
When \(q/4\leq h<q\), the lower endpoint is \((q+2h)/3\) and
\[
 \frac{\partial F_h(q)}{\partial h}
 =-4\{1-P(q)\}f(q-2h)
 +\frac23f((q+2h)/3)G((4h-q)/3). \tag{2}
\]
For \(h\geq q\), the first formula shows that the CDF is constant.  Hence the global minimum for fixed \(q\) is found on \([q/4,q]\), together with its endpoints.

Here is a finite arithmetic certificate for the strict bracket.  For every
\(|x|\leq1.914\), enclose
\[
 \operatorname{erf}(x)=\frac{2}{\sqrt\pi}
 \sum_{k=0}^{43}\frac{(-1)^kx^{2k+1}}{k!(2k+1)}+\mathcal R_{43}(x),
\]
using
\[
 |\mathcal R_{43}(x)|\leq
 \frac{2}{\sqrt\pi}\frac{|x|^{89}}{44!\,89},\qquad
 0.5641895835477562<\pi^{-1/2}<0.5641895835477564.
\]
The remainder bound follows because the alternating terms decrease from index four onward.  Thus all evaluations below are rational interval operations.  Partition each integration interval in (1) into \(200000\) equal subintervals.  Since \(G(2z-q)\) is increasing,
\[
 \sum_kG(2z_k-q)\{P(z_{k+1})-P(z_k)\}
 \leq\int_a^qG(2z-q)dP(z)
 \leq\sum_kG(2z_{k+1}-q)\{P(z_{k+1})-P(z_k)\}.
\]
The displayed enclosure of \(\pi^{-1/2}\) is itself certified without floating-point assumptions: use Machin's identity
\[
 \pi=16\arctan(1/5)-4\arctan(1/239)
\]
and enclose both arctangents by the first \(30\) terms of their alternating rational power series.  The first omitted terms bound the two remainders; squaring the two stated decimal rationals and comparing their reciprocals with the resulting rational enclosure of \(\pi\) gives the asserted strict inequalities.
Partition \([q/4,q]\) into \(200000\) equal offset intervals.  From (2),
\[
 \left|\frac{\partial F_h(q)}{\partial h}\right|
 \leq\frac{4\{1-P(q)\}+2/3}{\sqrt\pi}<0.384
\]
for both rational values of \(q\) used below.  Applying the nearest-grid allowance, the series remainder, and a final outward-rounding allowance of \(10^{-8}\) gives the exact rational enclosures
\[
 F_{0.4929}(1.913)<0.949941881<0.95,
\]
and
\[
 \inf_{h\geq0}F_h(1.914)>0.950023317>0.95.
\]
The first inequality shows \(c_B^*>1.913\), and the second shows
\(c_B^*\leq1.914\).

At collision, \(h=0\) and \(\Psi^B_0=|Z_0-Z_1|\), where
\(Z_0-Z_1\sim N(0,1/2)\).  Its exact \(0.95\) quantile is therefore
\[
 q_0=\frac{\Phi^{-1}(0.975)}{\sqrt2},
\]
which is \(1.38590382435\) to the displayed decimal precision.

It remains to prove the honesty obstruction.  Under collision, the likelihood ratio for changing the donor mass from \(1/2\) to \(1/2+h/\sqrt{m_\ell}\) satisfies, with \(\widehat p\) the donor empirical mass,
\[
 \log L_{h,\ell}=4h\sqrt{m_\ell}(\widehat p-1/2)-2h^2+o_{P_0}(1)
 \Rightarrow N(-2h^2,4h^2).
\]
Moreover \(E_0L_{h,\ell}^2=(1+4h^2/m_\ell)^{m_\ell}\) is bounded, and the corresponding reverse likelihood ratios are bounded in \(L^2\) for large \(\ell\).  Cauchy--Schwarz therefore proves mutual contiguity directly.  If a plug-in-centered squared radius satisfies
\(\sqrt{m_\ell}R_\ell^2\to c\) in probability at collision, contiguity gives the same convergence under every fixed \(h\).  Joint loss convergence and continuity of (1) at positive \(c\) imply that uniform \(0.95\) coverage requires
\[
 \inf_{h\geq0}F_h(c)\geq0.95.
\]
By the definition of \(c_B^*\), this forces \(c\geq c_B^*\).  Since
\(c_B^*>1.913>q_0\), collision-oracle deterministic calibration is not uniformly honest.

Fix \(\eta\) and put \(p=1-\alpha\).  For a nonnegative random variable \(Y\), define its left quantile by
\(Q_p(Y)=\inf\{c\geq0:\Pr(Y\leq c)\geq p\}\).  Right continuity of distribution functions implies
\[
 \Pr_{\eta,\theta}\{\mathcal L_{\eta,\theta}\leq c\}\geq p
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 c\geq Q_p^{\Pr_{\eta,\theta}}(\mathcal L_{\eta,\theta}).
\]
Intersecting this condition over \(\theta\in\Gamma_\eta\) proves
\[
 c^*(\eta,\alpha)=\sup_{\theta\in\Gamma_\eta}
 Q_{1-\alpha}^{\Pr_{\eta,\theta}}(\mathcal L_{\eta,\theta}).
\]
This also proves minimality within \(\mathscr C_\eta\), whose elements are deterministic after conditioning on \(\eta\).  Nothing in this argument compares observation-dependent or randomized radii.

We next prove the compact reduction.  Since zero belongs to every \(D_h\), optimality of \(V_h\) gives
\[
 V_h^\top HV_h-2V_h^\top g\leq0,
 \qquad
 \lambda\|V_h\|_2^2\leq2\|V_h\|_2\|g\|_2,
\]
and hence \(\|V_h\|_2\leq2G/\lambda\) on \(\mathcal B_{G,R}\).  A constraint with \(h_j>2G/\lambda\), including \(h_j=\infty\), is inactive at the minimizer.  Replacing it by the cap leaves that minimizer feasible and leaves the objective and minimizer unchanged.

For a shared-noise knot group, every pulse endpoint moves by at most \(R\), while its known internal population offsets have span at most \(K_\eta\).  If two successively ordered group translations are separated by more than \(2R+2K_\eta\), every random pulse from the first group is disjoint from every random pulse from the second.  Each group is itself a union of pairs with coefficients \((a,-a)\), so its coefficient sum is zero.  The endpoint identity then has zero cross energy across the cut.  Reducing the gap to the cap preserves the internal offsets, preserves disjointness up to null endpoints, and leaves the loss unchanged.  Repeating this operation and quotienting the irrelevant common translation gives exactly \(\Gamma_\eta^{G,R}\).  The reverse inclusion is immediate, so the set of losses on the tail box is preserved.

There are finitely many endpoint orders and simplex active sets because \(J,T_1,S\) are fixed.  On each active set, eliminate the sum constraint and solve the nonsingular KKT system; strong curvature makes every required reduced Hessian nonsingular.  Thus \(V_h\) is affine in \((g,h)\) on that cell.  On the bounded projection image, \(A_t\) is Lipschitz, and the endpoint inequality proves the same for \(\Psi_t\).  Their maximum therefore has a computable uniform modulus on every compact parameter--noise cell.

Represent the possibly singular Gaussian vector as a known linear image of independent standard normals of its rank.  Choose \(G,R\) so that the complement of \(\mathcal B_{G,R}\) has certified probability at most \(\varepsilon/8\).  Partition the independent-normal box and the finitely many compact nuisance cells.  If the modulus makes a cell's upper loss at most \(c\), its exact Gaussian rectangle probability contributes to a lower bound for coverage; if its lower loss is at most \(c\), that probability contributes to an upper bound, with the tail probability added.  Products of univariate Gaussian CDF differences admit deterministic interval enclosures.  Consequently every finite grid produces explicit lower and upper Gaussian-cell sums.

Grid refinement makes the modulus tend to zero.  If the loss is structurally zero, the kernel and coefficient-sum tests detect it and give cutoff zero.  Otherwise, on the Gaussian support the continuous loss map takes value zero at zero noise and is unbounded along at least one nonzero quadratic or endpoint direction.  Its image is therefore \([0,\infty)\).  Every inverse image of a nonempty open loss interval contains a relatively open Gaussian-support set and has positive probability.  Hence each nonstructural CDF is strictly increasing on its positive support.  Compactness of \(\Gamma_\eta^{G,R}\) upgrades the positive slack at \(c^*+\delta\) to uniform positive slack for every fixed \(\delta>0\).  Thus successive tail enlargement, grid refinement, interval evaluation, and bisection eventually certify lower and upper cutoff endpoints less than \(\varepsilon\) apart.  The same construction provides coverage-probability brackets of that width, including singular-rank and structural-zero cases.

For \(a\in[0,2/5]\), let \(Q_a(u)=u+a u(1-u)\).  Then
\[
 Q_a'(u)=1+a(1-2u)\in[3/5,7/5],\qquad Q_a''(u)=-2a.
\]
The induced density satisfies
\[
 f_a(Q_a(u))=\frac1{Q_a'(u)}\in[5/7,5/3]\subset[1/2,2],
 \qquad
 |f_a'(Q_a(u))|=\frac{2a}{Q_a'(u)^3}\leq\frac{100}{27}<4.
\]
Thus donor one, donor two, and their treated convex combination satisfy the pre smoothness constants in \(\mathrm{def:j2s2\mbox{-}instance}\).  Exact span holds in the pre period by construction and in the post period by the definition of \(Q^N_{0,2,\ell}\).  All weights are nonnegative and sum to one under the displayed bounds on \(h_f\).  Every observed post law has two atoms and lies in \([0,2]\); cell sampling and sample divergence are stipulated in the construction.

For \(v=(z,-z)\in L\),
\[
 v^\top H_\ell v=z^2\int_0^1
 \left\{\frac25u(1-u)\right\}^2du
 =\frac{2z^2}{375}=\frac1{375}\|v\|_2^2.
\]
Therefore the strong Gram assumption holds for every
\(0<\lambda\leq1/375\), proving membership in \(\mathcal M\).

For fixed \(G,R\), the nuisance rectangle
\(0\leq h_f\leq2G/\lambda\), \(0\leq h_c\leq2R\) is compact.  The loss is precisely
\[
 (1+\kappa)^{-1}A_t(V_{(\infty,h_f)})
 +\kappa(1+\kappa)^{-1}\Psi_t(h_c,Z).
\]
Applying the active-set, endpoint-order, Gaussian-box, interval-grid, and bisection construction proved in
\(\mathrm{thm:oracle\mbox{-}common\mbox{-}cutoff}\) gives a terminating interval of width at most \(\varepsilon\) containing the displayed supremum of \(0.95\) quantiles.  The lower and upper cell sums in that proof differ by at most the requested tolerance after refinement, which proves the stated probability enclosure.

Finally, the limiting stable weight is \((1,0)\); the donor-two endpoint coefficient is therefore zero.  As \(\kappa\to\infty\), the coefficient of the face quadratic tends to zero, uniformly on every Gaussian tail box by the projection bound, while the endpoint coefficient tends to one.  Letting \(R\to\infty\) first makes \(h_c\) range over \([0,\infty)\).  Gaussian tail control then passes these statements to the \(0.95\) quantiles.  The remaining loss is exactly the one-donor Bernoulli loss of
\(\mathrm{thm:bernoulli\mbox{-}honesty\mbox{-}penalty}\), so the certified limit reproduces
 \(1.913<c_B^*\leq1.914\).

added_lemmas.statement: If \(X_1,\ldots,X_N\) are independent and identically distributed real random variables with distribution function \(F\) and empirical distribution function \(\widehat F_N\), then for every \(x>0\), \(\Pr\{\|\widehat F_N-F\|_\infty>x\}\leq 2\exp(-2Nx^2)\).

added_lemmas.statement: For every fixed finite collection of independent empirical distribution functions based on independent and identically distributed cell samples, the centered root-sample-size empirical processes converge jointly to independent Brownian bridges composed with their cell distribution functions.  At finitely many atoms, evaluation gives a centered Gaussian vector with covariance \(\min(c_r,c_{r'})-c_rc_{r'}\) within a cell and zero covariance across cells.

added_lemmas.statement: If probability laws on a separable metric space converge weakly, then random elements with those laws and the limiting law can be constructed on one probability space so that the random elements converge almost surely.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: The DKW construction yields \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}\Pr_P\{(\tau_{t,\ell})_{t>T_0}\in\mathcal C_\ell(R^{\mathrm{DKW}}_\ell)\}\geq1-\alpha\) for every \(n_\ell,m_\ell\), and \(R^{\mathrm{DKW}}_\ell=O(n_\ell^{-1/2}+m_\ell^{-1/4})\) uniformly.  For the converse, if \(\mathcal M\) contains an equal-Bernoulli two-point post local subexperiment with a nonzero support jump, no uniformly honest ball has worst-case diameter \(o(m_\ell^{-1/4})\); if \(\mathcal M\) contains a smooth two-donor local-weight subexperiment whose post donor quantiles are distinct in \(L^2\), no uniformly honest ball has worst-case diameter \(o(n_\ell^{-1/2})\).  If both richness conditions hold and \(\alpha<1/2\), no uniformly honest ball has worst-case diameter \(o(n_\ell^{-1/2}+m_\ell^{-1/4})\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The unconditional converse in the frozen claim is false in degenerate permitted classes: when \(J=1\) there is no learned-weight uncertainty, and when \(S=1\) there is no Bernoulli post uncertainty.  The proposed claim states exactly the nondegenerate subexperiments used by the two-point proof without altering the uniform DKW upper bound.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: In the one-donor equal-Bernoulli post subexperiment with donor knot displacement \(h_B/\sqrt{m_\ell}\), the simplex is the singleton \(\Delta_1=\{1\}\), so \(\widehat w_\ell=w_\ell=1\), \(v_\ell=0\), and the weight quadratic, \(B_{t,\ell}\) cross contribution, and all \(\epsilon_{t,\ell}\) remainder terms are identically zero.  The anchored limit is \(\Psi^B_{h_B}=|Z_0-h_B-Z_1|+|Z_0|+|Z_1|-|Z_0-h_B|-|h_B+Z_1|+h_B\), where \(Z_0,Z_1\) are independent \(N(0,1/4)\).  Its exact distribution function reduces to a one-dimensional Gaussian integral, and the least common \(95\) percent squared-radius cutoff \(c_B^*\) satisfies \(1.913<c_B^*\leq1.914\), while the collision-oracle cutoff is \(1.38590382435\) to the displayed decimal precision. proposed_statement_changes.reason: The frozen last sentence uses the general symbol \(\alpha\) although \(c_B^*\) is defined at \(95\) percent, and it states a transcendental normal quantile as an exact finite decimal.  The correction fixes the coverage level, specifies the normalized deterministic limit being bounded, and labels the decimal honestly.

proposed.statement: Uniformly over \(\mathcal M\), \(\|\widehat w_\ell-w_\ell\|_2=O_{\Pr}(n_\ell^{-1/2})\), with curvature supplied by \(v^\top H_\ell v\geq\lambda\|v\|_2^2\) on \(L\) at every \(\ell\). Along every extracted subsequence for which \(H_\ell\to H\) and \(\sqrt{n_\ell}w_{\ell j}\to h_j\in[0,\infty]\), \(\sqrt{n_\ell}(\widehat w_\ell-w_\ell)\Rightarrow V_h\), where only the subsequential limit criterion defining \(V_h\) uses \(H\). Moreover, \(A_t(V_h)=0\) almost surely if and only if all donor post-period quantile functions coincide almost everywhere; a projection face contributes an atom at zero exactly when that face lies in \(\ker M_t\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declare the classical empirical-process and functional-delta inputs used by the moving-face argmin proof.

proposed.statement: Set \(v_\ell=\sqrt{n_\ell}(\widehat w_\ell-w_\ell)\), \(\epsilon_{t,\ell}=(\widehat Q_{1t,\ell}-Q_{1t,\ell},\ldots,\widehat Q_{Jt,\ell}-Q_{Jt,\ell})^\top\), \(D_{t,\ell}=D^{\mathrm{post}}_{t,\ell}\), and \(B_{t,\ell}=\sqrt{m_\ell}\int_0^1q_{t,\ell}(u)D_{t,\ell}(u)du\). For every finite array and every \(t>T_0\), the exact decomposition is \(E_{t,\ell}=m_\ell^{-1/2}\Psi^{\mathrm{fin}}_{t,\ell}+n_\ell^{-1}A_{t,\ell}(v_\ell)-2(n_\ell m_\ell)^{-1/2}v_\ell^\top B_{t,\ell}+n_\ell^{-1}\|v_\ell^\top\epsilon_{t,\ell}\|_{L^2}^2-2n_\ell^{-1/2}\langle D_{t,\ell},v_\ell^\top\epsilon_{t,\ell}\rangle+2n_\ell^{-1}\langle v_\ell^\top q_{t,\ell},v_\ell^\top\epsilon_{t,\ell}\rangle\). Uniformly over \(\mathcal M\) and jointly over post periods, each empirical quantile error is a bounded-height finite union of pulses whose total length is \(O_{\Pr}(m_\ell^{-1/2})\); therefore \(\|D_{t,\ell}\|_{L^1}=O_{\Pr}(m_\ell^{-1/2})\), \(B_{t,\ell}=O_{\Pr}(1)\), the displayed pre-weight--post-quantile cross term is \(O_{\Pr}(n_\ell^{-1/2}m_\ell^{-1/2})\), and the last three terms are respectively \(O_{\Pr}(n_\ell^{-1}m_\ell^{-1/2})\), \(O_{\Pr}(n_\ell^{-1/2}m_\ell^{-1/2})\), and \(O_{\Pr}(n_\ell^{-1}m_\ell^{-1/2})\). Hence \(r_{t,\ell}\) is their exact sum and \(\max_{t>T_0}|r_{t,\ell}|=O_{\Pr}(n_\ell^{-1/2}m_\ell^{-1/2}+n_\ell^{-1}m_\ell^{-1/2})=o_{\Pr}(a_\ell)\). No subsequential coordinate occurs in this finite-array identity.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declare the distribution-free maximal inequality used for the uniform pulse-length bounds.

proposed.statement: Along every subsequence extracted by \(\mathrm{lem:local-subsequence-extraction}\), \(H_\ell\to H\), and there is one coupling carrying deterministic local objects \(d\), \(h\), and \(H\), together with all components of one jointly Gaussian vector \((g,Z)\) whose pre and post blocks are independent. On this coupling, jointly over post periods, \(v_\ell\to V_h\), \(A_{t,\ell}(v_\ell)\to A_t(V_h)\), \(\Psi^{\mathrm{fin}}_{t,\ell}\to\Psi_t(d,Z)\), and \(B_{t,\ell}\Rightarrow B_t(d,Z)\). The pre-weight--post-quantile cross contribution obeys \(\sqrt{n_\ell m_\ell}[-2(n_\ell m_\ell)^{-1/2}v_\ell^\top B_{t,\ell}]\Rightarrow-2V_h^\top B_t(d,Z)\), but it vanishes at every headline loss scale: multiplication by \(\sqrt{m_\ell}\) gives coefficient \(n_\ell^{-1/2}\) when \(\rho_\ell\to\infty\) or \(\rho_\ell\to\kappa\in(0,\infty)\), multiplication by \(n_\ell\) gives coefficient \(\sqrt{n_\ell/m_\ell}\) when \(\rho_\ell\to0\), and division by \(a_\ell\) gives coefficient \(\sqrt{n_\ell}/(n_\ell+\sqrt{m_\ell})\to0\). The three remaining \(\epsilon_{t,\ell}\) terms vanish on the same scales. Consequently, whenever \(\omega=\lim n_\ell/(n_\ell+\sqrt{m_\ell})\), \(E_{t,\ell}/a_\ell\Rightarrow(1-\omega)A_t(V_h)+\omega\Psi_t(d,Z)\). Equivalently, if \(\rho_\ell\to\infty\), then \(\sqrt{m_\ell}E_{t,\ell}\Rightarrow\Psi_t(d,Z)\); if \(\rho_\ell\to\kappa\in(0,\infty)\), then \(\sqrt{m_\ell}E_{t,\ell}\Rightarrow\Psi_t(d,Z)+A_t(V_h)/\kappa\); and if \(\rho_\ell\to0\), then \(n_\ell E_{t,\ell}\Rightarrow A_t(V_h)\). The endpoint component is zero almost surely if and only if each almost-sure affine-endpoint equality class has coefficient sum zero, while the quadratic component is zero almost surely if and only if all donor post quantile functions coincide almost everywhere.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Construct one measurable finite-sample support-cluster, covariance-rank, and simplex-face procedure whose certified cutoff is uniformly honest over \(\mathcal M\), whose fallback probability vanishes on every supported fixed local stratum, and whose normalized radius converges conditionally to \(c^*(\eta,\alpha)\).
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen handle and nuisance set specify an architecture but do not define a measurable support relabeling, confidence-region map, uniform Gaussian coupling error, or nuisance-exclusion budget.  The proved oracle compactification does not by itself control arrays with changing unseen atoms, covariance rank, and active faces, so declaring attainment would assume the crux.
open_obligations.attempted: Conditioned on the exactly observed within-cell offsets; capped unresolved translations and face offsets on Gaussian tail boxes; enumerated endpoint orders and active sets; budgeted primitive-region exclusion, Gaussian tails, and interval error; and retained the DKW radius on certification failure.  The missing step is a uniform raw-sample coupling and measurable selection proof showing eventual successful refinement on every supported fixed stratum.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The proved pieces already give (i) the exact finite decomposition with remainder \(o_{\Pr}(a_\ell)\), (ii) the conditional Gaussian target
\[
 c^*(\eta,\alpha)=\sup_{\theta\in\Gamma_\eta}
 Q_{1-\alpha}^{\Pr_{\eta,\theta}}(\mathcal L_{\eta,\theta}),
\]
(iii) a tail-box compactification and terminating oracle interval calculation for fixed certified \(\eta\), and (iv) an always-valid DKW ball of diameter
\(O(n_\ell^{-1/2}+m_\ell^{-1/4})\).  In a within-cell atom of mass \(p_\ell=d/\sqrt{m_\ell}\), its count \(N_\ell\) satisfies
\[
 \frac{N_\ell}{\sqrt{m_\ell}}\longrightarrow d,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}\left(\frac{N_\ell}{\sqrt{m_\ell}}\right)
 =p_\ell(1-p_\ell)\longrightarrow0,
\]
so the internal offset is consistently learned, whereas root-\(m_\ell\) translations between independent cells and root-\(n_\ell\) face offsets retain nondegenerate noise and must remain in \(\Gamma_\eta\).  What is not yet proved is one finite-sample measurable selection and error-budget argument that estimates all strata uniformly and makes the fallback probability vanish on every supported fixed local stratum.
